renderingModel.observation: open shadowRoot parts (group-header, option, no-results), host attributes (data-open), the emptyStateChange CustomEvent detail, public lifecycle callbacks (callbacks.onOpen), and getEmptyStateContext

No browser-only oracle was identified (unlike ATTR-021, whose closing motion requires real stylesheet-resolved animation). jsdomTests: API-002: default is undefined; setting a renderer is returned by the getter and drives group headers
API-002: identity-preserving assignment keeps the same instance (public stability, not an internal-return proof)
API-002: replacement re-renders headers from the new renderer; clearing restores the default label
API-002.observable: getter returns the assigned reference; the assigned renderer's element becomes the group-header part (part="group-header", class group-header, role="presentation" unless set, renderer dataset preserved); re-assigning the SAME reference keeps both the public function identity and the same rendered header node; replacing with a new renderer re-renders; assigning undefined restores the default plain-label header
positivePaths: set renderer -> getter returns it -> rendered header carries the renderer output (dataset/role/class)
identity-preserving re-assign -> same function ref AND same header node (public stability)
replace renderer -> getter returns replacement -> header re-rendered from it (A:G1 -> B:G1)
negativePaths: clear (undefined) -> getter undefined -> default plain-label header (G1)
API-002.scopeNote: Equal-identity assignment proves PUBLIC stability (observable function identity + stable rendered node). It does NOT by itself prove the internal early-return branch (setter line 502); that branch is a private implementation detail and is deliberately not asserted. The distinction is documented here so the characterization is not over-claimed.

jsdomTests: EVENT-011: searching to no results emits {context:{query,reason:no-results}} and exposes it via getEmptyStateContext
EVENT-011: a repeated identical query emits NO duplicate (no state change)
EVENT-011: clearing the query transitions context back to null (real state change)
EVENT-011: empty item set reports no-options; populated set clears the context (negative)
EVENT-011.observable: the emptyStateChange CustomEvent detail is exactly {context:{query,reason}} on a non-empty empty state, or {context:null} when the empty state clears; reason is 'no-options' (no items) or 'no-results' (search filtered all items); getEmptyStateContext() returns a frozen snapshot with exactly the keys query+reason
EVENT-011.payloadShapePreserved: { context: { query: string, reason: 'no-options'|'no-results' } } | { context: null } — asserted exactly, preserving the accepted public payload
positivePaths: search to no results -> exactly one {context:{query:'zzz',reason:'no-results'}}; getEmptyStateContext equal + frozen + keys [query,reason]
negativePaths: repeated identical query -> NO new emptyStateChange (a real state-change boundary; only transitions emit)
EVENT-011.duplicateBoundary: The duplicate boundary distinguishes a REAL transition from a no-op re-notification: emitting the same effective context twice yields exactly one event; clearing to null is a distinct transition that DOES emit.
EVENT-011.drivingNote: Driven via the PUBLIC search input (input[part="input"] value + input event with searchable:true). This deliberately avoids the private _handleSearch used by the pre-existing empty-state-slot.spec.ts, so T3 characterizes the event on the public surface only.

jsdomTests: LIFECYCLE-002: after connect an outside pointerdown closes an open popup (document-listener effect)
LIFECYCLE-002: connecting fires the public onOpen lifecycle callback once
LIFECYCLE-002.observable: after connect, with the popup open (host data-open="true"), an outside document pointerdown closes it (data-open removed); connecting fires the public callbacks.onOpen exactly once
positivePaths: connect -> open() -> data-open="true" -> outside pointerdown -> data-open removed (document-listener effect observed)
connect -> onOpen callback invoked exactly once
LIFECYCLE-002.scopeNote: Characterizes the OBSERVED public effects of connection (document-listener effect + onOpen callback). It does not claim any internal ownership/registration detail beyond the observable effect. onOpen fires on both connect and open(); the once-on-connect assertion drives a single connect without an intervening open, isolating connect.
claimsNotEstablished: Does not prove a specific number of internal document listeners or their registration identity — only that outside input closes the open popup after connect.

jsdomTests: LIFECYCLE-003: disconnecting closes an open popup and releases rendered options from the shadow tree
LIFECYCLE-003: after disconnect the detached element remains closed and detached on outside input
LIFECYCLE-003.observable: on remove() while open: the popup closes (data-open removed) and rendered option nodes are released from the shadow tree (0 [part="option"]); after disconnect the element reports isConnected=false and, on a subsequent outside pointerdown, remains closed (no unexpected state change / no re-open)
positivePaths: remove() while open -> data-open removed AND 0 rendered [part="option"] (released)
after remove() -> element is detached (isConnected=false) and remains closed on outside pointerdown
negativePaths: outside pointerdown after disconnect does not re-open the detached element
LIFECYCLE-003.scopeNote: Narrowed per T3-F01. Characterizes only the OBSERVED public effects of disconnection: popup closure, rendered-option release, detached state, and no unexpected state change on outside input. The test records the post-disconnect closed pre-condition before dispatching input so the post-input assertion is not vacuous.
claimsNotEstablished: Does NOT prove that a document event listener was removed/aborted — the popup is already closed post-disconnect, so remaining closed after outside input is consistent with either removed listeners or an already-closed component.
Does NOT prove internal resource/cardinality release beyond what is externally observable (popup closed + zero rendered [part="option"] + detached).

jsdomTests: LIFECYCLE-004: reconnecting re-renders each item exactly once (no duplicated render effects)
LIFECYCLE-004: after reconnect outside input still closes the popup, once per open (observable invariant)
LIFECYCLE-004.observable: remove()+appendChild re-renders each item exactly once (option count equals item count, data-value ['a','b'] — not doubled); after reconnect an outside pointerdown closes the popup emitting exactly one public `close` event per open, and a second open/close cycle likewise emits exactly one close per open
positivePaths: reconnect -> option count == item count (not doubled); distinct nodes with data-value ['a','b']
reconnect -> open() -> outside pointerdown -> closed with exactly one `close` event; second cycle -> exactly one more `close` event
negativePaths: reconnect does NOT double the rendered options
close events do NOT accumulate beyond one per open across cycles
LIFECYCLE-004.invariant: Observable reconnection invariant: reconnection restores rendering (no duplicated option nodes) and outside-input closing still works with exactly one public `close` event per open across repeated cycles.
LIFECYCLE-004.scopeNote: Narrowed per T3-F02. This is an OBSERVABLE invariant, strengthened with a public `close`-event count, not a proof of exactly one internal document listener. Two internal listeners could produce the same single `close` observable if the second handler encounters an already-closed component, so listener cardinality is explicitly NOT claimed.
claimsNotEstablished: Does NOT prove exactly one internal document listener exists after reconnect (duplicate listeners facing an already-closed popup would observe the same single `close`).
The public `close`-event count strengthens the behavioral contract but does not establish internal listener uniqueness.

jsdomTests: CONFIG-023: expandable.enabled=true renders no expand/collapse UI and exposes no public expand control
CONFIG-023: toggling expandable.enabled at runtime produces no observable DOM change (unwired negative)
CONFIG-023.gap: The public `expandable` config (ExpandableConfig: enabled/collapsedHeight/expandedHeight/expandLabel/collapseLabel) is DECLARED and defaulted in the global config but is NOT wired to the component. Verification: `grep -rn 'expandable|Expandable' packages/core/src` (excluding tests) returns ONLY global-config.ts declaration (interface line 62, config field 305, defaults 406) and has ZERO usages in enhanced-select.ts or any component/logic path. `updateConfig({expandable:{enabled:true}})` is accepted silently with no public effect.
CONFIG-023.observable: with expandable.enabled=true and the popup open: no expand/collapse part or element renders (no part containing 'expand', no [data-expand], no [class*=expand]); the capabilities report contains no 'expand' feature; toggling expandable.enabled at runtime produces byte-identical shadowRoot innerHTML
negativePaths: enable expandable -> no expand UI, no expand part token, capabilities report has no 'expand' (unwired)
runtime toggle enabled false->true -> identical shadowRoot innerHTML (inert on the public surface)
CONFIG-023.decision: KEEP Missing with this explicit gap. The config has no public effect to characterize; making it observable requires production wiring (out of Task 3 scope — no production remediation). Deferred for reconciliation at W1-P1.4 closure, analogous to the documented PART-009 gap.

corrections.finding: The LIFECYCLE-003 disconnect test dispatched a document pointerdown after disconnecting and asserted the component stayed closed, and the evidence claimed the document listener was 'no longer acting' / 'removed'. Because the component was already closed on disconnect, remaining closed does not independently prove listener removal. Characterization evidence must not substitute source inspection for public behavior.
corrections.resolution: Narrowed the test title/comment and evidence to the observable assertions actually established: popup closure, rendered-option release (0 [part="option"]), detached state (isConnected=false), and no unexpected state change on outside input. The test now records the post-disconnect closed pre-condition before dispatching input so the post-input assertion is not vacuous. Added explicit claimsNotEstablished stating listener removal is not black-box proven. Source inspection (controller abort) is NOT used as a substitute claim.

corrections.finding: LIFECYCLE-004 asserted that a single outside press 'closes once' and the evidence claimed duplicate listeners would cause repeated/nondeterministic closures. Two document listeners could produce the same observable result if the first closes the popup and the second encounters an already-closed component, so internal listener uniqueness is not established.
corrections.resolution: Retitled and rewrote the test as an observable reconnection invariant: after reconnect, rendering is restored without duplication and outside input closes the popup with exactly one public `close` event per open across two cycles. Added explicit claimsNotEstablished stating listener cardinality is not proven (the public close count strengthens the behavioral contract but does not establish internal listener uniqueness).
